```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(easyNIS)
```

## Choose comparable years

The 2012 NIS redesign changed the sampling unit from hospitals to discharges.
Use `DISCWT` from 2012 onward. For a study that crosses the redesign, HCUP
specifies replacement `TRENDWT` for 1993–2011 and `DISCWT` from 2012 onward.
The easyNIS trend workflow starts in 2012. The survey design scopes both
`HOSP_NIS` and `NIS_STRATUM` by year. Hospital numbers can recur across releases
and cannot identify the same hospital over time.
[Introduction to the NIS](https://hcup-us.ahrq.gov/db/nation/nis/NIS_Introduction_2021.jsp),
[2012 redesign, Methods Series 2014-04](https://hcup-us.ahrq.gov/reports/methods/2014-04.pdf),
[NIS trend weights](https://hcup-us.ahrq.gov/db/nation/nis/trendwghts.jsp).

2015 Q1–Q3 use ICD-9-CM and Q4 uses ICD-10-CM/PCS. For a diagnosis- or
procedure-based cohort or outcome, start with complete years within one
coding era (2012–2014 or 2016 onward). Run separate analyses to describe both
eras. If a study must include the transition, examine quarterly frequencies
for discontinuities and report how the definition and coverage change. Read
HCUP's recommendations before combining quarters or fitting a model across
the break. For coding-independent analyses, such as total adult discharges
using age alone, `coding = "independent"` allows complete 2015 data and years
on both sides. The argument records the analyst's choice.
[HCUP recommendations for reporting trends](https://hcup-us.ahrq.gov/datainnovations/HCUP_RecomForReportingTrends_070517.pdf).

Check the Known Data Issues section for corrections to the releases you
use, including the notices for 2019–2020. Check the annual introductions
for changes to variable availability and definitions.
[NIS Database Documentation](https://hcup-us.ahrq.gov/db/nation/nis/nisdbdocumentation.jsp).

## Estimate a total for each year

Open the complete annual samples and pass the cohort as a logical expression.
`nis_annual_totals()` uses each year's original discharge weights. It checks
whether all four quarter labels are represented in each input year. Verify
sample completeness separately. Missing estimates identify years with no
valid cohort discharges in the design. Review data and cohort coverage before
interpreting those years.

```{r annual}
nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2018:2020)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50")

nis_annual_totals(nis, heart_failure)
```

Report the calendar years, cohort definition, weight, and design used to
compute standard errors. Apply [disclosure rules](disclosure.html) before
sharing estimates, plots, or tests. The examples use invented discharges.

## Estimate an average annual total

If the target is the **average annual number** of cohort discharges over
the included complete years, pool with `annualize = TRUE`. This divides the
weights by the number of included years, scaling both the pooled total and
its standard error. A year without cohort discharges still contributes to
the divisor. Use `annualize = FALSE` for the cumulative total across those
years. A pooled weighted mean or proportion describes the pooled discharge
population. Dividing every weight by the same number leaves it unchanged.
Report the denominator in proportions, for example all eligible discharges
for a share of NIS discharges.

```{r pooled}
pooled <- nis_design(nis, heart_failure, keep = LOS, annualize = TRUE)
srvyr::summarise(pooled, annual_discharges = srvyr::survey_total())
```

## Test for linear change in an outcome

Define the outcome and the time scale before fitting a trend. For example,
use survey-weighted regression to estimate the change in mean length of
stay per calendar year among heart failure discharges. Center calendar year
to make the intercept the fitted mean for the first year. Calendar-time
spacing is preserved when included years have gaps.

```{r slope}
design <- nis_design(nis, heart_failure, keep = LOS) |>
  dplyr::mutate(elapsed = YEAR - 2018L)

fit <- survey::svyglm(LOS ~ elapsed, design = design)
summary(fit)$coefficients["elapsed", ]
```

The coefficient and its design-based uncertainty describe change in mean
length of stay, measured in days per year. Choose a model and denominator
that match the outcome. For a binary outcome, a quasibinomial survey model
with numeric year estimates linear change on the log-odds scale. For
year-specific comparisons, specify year as a factor. Changes in case mix,
coding, and practice can all affect the slope. A discharge-level outcome
model answers a different question from a time-series model for annual
national volumes.
[HCUP trend methods, Methods Series 2006-05](https://hcup-us.ahrq.gov/reports/methods/2006_05_NISTrendsReport_1988-2004A.pdf),
[Variance estimation, Methods Series 2015-09](https://hcup-us.ahrq.gov/reports/methods/2015_09.jsp).

Published NIS studies illustrate how to report the choice of estimand and
methods. Alkhouli and colleagues specified the calendar periods and
distinguished trend tests for categorical and continuous outcomes. The study
of surgical treatment for pseudotumor cerebri reported annual procedure
counts and described its survey regression and coding-era adjustment.
[Alkhouli et al., JAMA Network Open (2020)](https://doi.org/10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2019.21326),
[JAMA Ophthalmology study (2020)](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamaophthalmology/fullarticle/2774167).
